LightCraft 

 Your photos. Your pixels. Your machine. 

 
 English ·
 简体中文 ·
 繁體中文 
 

 
 Photo library and raw development; an open-source, non-destructive photo library and raw developer, built in pure Rust. 
 Native on macOS, Windows and Linux. In the browser via WebAssembly. Drivable end to end by AI agents over MCP.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 LightCraft on getartcraft.com ·
 ArtCraft ·
 All Crafting Apps 
 

 

 
 
 
 Ansel Adams, "The Tetons and the Snake River" (1942). Public domain, U.S. National Archives. Developed in LightCraft. 
 

 [!NOTE]
 ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life. Digital, generative, music,
 games — if you make things, you're one of us. Come say hi on Discord. 

 
 Editing ·
 Color grading ·
 Before & after ·
 Masking ·
 Presets ·
 Library ·
 Agents & MCP ·
 Performance ·
 Status ·
 Quick start ·
 Roadmap ·
 Downloads ·
 Crafting Apps 
 

 

 Edit like you mean it

LightCraft is a complete darkroom in a single native app. Every adjustment is non-destructive , so your originals
are never touched. Every slider renders through a scene-referred, wide-gamut, 32-bit float pipeline : highlights
roll off like film, shadows open up without halos, and colour stays clean from capture to export.

 
 
 

 ☀️ Light
 Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks , with edge-aware local tone mapping (a guided filter on
log-luminance). Pulling −100 Highlights recovers a blown sky without the grey halos you'd get from a naive curve.

 🎨 Color
 White balance by temperature and tint (Kelvin for raw, relative for JPEG) with presets, Auto and a
click-to-neutralise eyedropper . Vibrance that protects skin tones, Saturation , an 8-band Color Mixer 
(hue / saturation / luminance) and 3-way Color Grading wheels with blending and balance. All of it is computed in
OkLCh, a modern perceptual colour space.

 
 

 ✨ Effects
 Texture for fine detail, Clarity for mid-tone punch, Dehaze (dark-channel prior with guided refinement;
push it negative to add atmosphere), post-crop Vignette with highlight priority, roundness and feather, and
resolution-independent film Grain with size and roughness.

 📈 Tone Curve
Parametric region curve with movable splits plus point curves for RGB, Red, Green and Blue. Curves are monotone by
construction, so you never get an accidental tone inversion.

 
 
 

 
 
 
 A gentle S on the RGB point curve, right under the Light sliders. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain). 
 

 

 Color grading, the cinematic way

Split-tone shadows, midtones and highlights independently with drag-anywhere colour wheels. Below, Dorothea Lange's
 Migrant Mother gets a warm, print-like tone (highlights at 42°, shadows at 28°) in two drags.

 
 
 
 Shadows, midtones and highlights wheels in the Color panel. Dorothea Lange, "Migrant Mother" (1936). Public domain, Library of Congress. 
 

 

 Before & after

Press \\ to toggle the Before view, Y for side by side, or Shift + Y for a
split view. Every image below is a real screenshot of LightCraft, captured automatically by an agent through the
control channel.

 
 
 The Tetons and the Snake River. Highlights −45, Shadows +38, Clarity +28, Dehaze +18. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain). 
 Migrant Mother. Shadows +42, Texture +18, split-toned grade, vignette. Dorothea Lange, 1936 (public domain). 
 
 
 Earthrise. Dehaze +22, Highlights −30, warmer white balance, Vibrance +22. NASA / Bill Anders, Apollo 8, 1968 (public domain). 
 The Blue Marble. Highlights −38, Blacks −20, Dehaze +15, Vibrance +30. NASA, Apollo 17, 1972 (public domain). 
 
 

 

 Masking that goes where you point

Paint with a Brush (size, feather, flow, density, erase), drop Linear and Radial Gradients with draggable
pins, or select by Luminance Range , Color Range , Sky , Subject and Background . Combine components
with Add / Subtract / Intersect , invert any of them, and dial in 17 local adjustments per mask (Temp, Tint,
Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Hue, Saturation, Sharpness, Noise,
Moiré, Defringe), plus an overall Amount.

Desktop Object and Describe masks use SAM 3 for click-based and text-prompt selection, with a separately
installed model; see model setup and terms. Subject, Sky and Background selections still use
classical heuristics. Existing model-generated masks render and export without the model installed.

 
 
 
 A radial "Sun glow" mask (Temp +40, Exposure +0.50) layered over a linear "Sky" mask. Photo from LightCraft's procedurally generated demo library. 
 

 

 Presets, profiles & the Color Mixer

Forty-one hand-built presets ship in the box ( Golden Hour, Teal & Orange, Faded Matte, Selenium Tone, Crisp
Landscape and more), each with an Amount slider from 0 to 200 %. Save your own from any group of settings, mark
favourites, and copy, paste or sync edits across a whole selection with exactly the groups you choose.

 
 
 
 The Presets column next to the 8-band Color Mixer. Photo from the demo library. 
 

 
 
 

 ✂️ Crop, straighten & geometry
Free or locked aspect ratios (1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 4:3, 16:9, 16:10, original), drag-to-rotate straightening that always
keeps the largest crop inside the image, thirds / grid / golden-ratio overlays, flips and 90° rotations, plus
manual Vertical, Horizontal, Rotate, Aspect, Scale and Offset transforms.

 
 

 ⚫️ Black & White
One click ( V ) to monochrome, with an 8-band B&W Mix that lets you darken skies or make foliage glow.
Then tone it with Color Grading for selenium, sepia or split-tone prints.

 
 
 
 A 16:9 crop straightened +2.5° with the thirds overlay. Ansel Adams, 1942 (public domain). 
 Split view: colour original on the left, B&W with Clarity, Vignette and Grain on the right. Demo library. 
 
 

 

 Organize everything

A library that stays out of your way: All Photos , Recently Added , Picks , By Date , Albums nested in
 Folders , and Recently Deleted . Rate with 0 – 5 , flag with P / X /
 U , colour-la

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Workspace builds, including the desktop, web and CLI applications, require Rust 1.95 or newer.

git clone https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft && cd lightcraft
cargo run --release -p lightcraft                       # opens your library (~/Pictures/LightCraft Library; a new one starts with demo photos)
cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- ~/Pictures/trip    # import your photos (folders are scanned, duplicates skipped)
cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- --memory           # a throwaway in-memory demo session (writes nothing)
cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- --control 7980     # with the automation channel
cargo xtask web --serve                                 # the same app in the browser: http://127.0.0.1:8080/
cargo run --release -p lightcraft-cli -- render photo.jpg -o out.jpg --set light.exposure=0.5
cargo xtask ci                                          # fmt, clippy, HEIF, tests, parity, layers, assets, WASM
cargo xtask ci --quick                                  # only what your branch's changes can break (minutes)

cargo xtask ci --quick compares with the merge base of origin/main (--base REF for another) and runs fmt, clippy, the tests of the changed packages, layers and assets, plus HEIF, parity and the wasm check when the changes touch them; a change to Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or the lint config tests everything. GitHub runs the full cargo xtask ci on every pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Only one ci runs at a time per machine: a second one, from another worktree say, waits for the first and names it, since several at once take longer in total than in turn. LIGHTCRAFT_CI_SLOTS=2 allows two; LIGHTCRAFT_CI_LOCK=off skips the lock.

CI defaults to line-table debug information and one build job per 1.5 GB of RAM available when it starts (at most one per CPU; 4 if memory can't be read), so an 8 GB machine with 6 GB free builds with 4, and a busy machine with little free builds with fewer. Test threads follow, capped at 4. Full-debuginfo linkers, one per CPU, otherwise exhaust RAM before any test runs. GPU coverage is unchanged. Explicit CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, RUST_TEST_THREADS and NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS settings override these defaults. The tests run under cargo test; LIGHTCRAFT_NEXTEST=1 runs them under cargo-nextest instead (one process per test, slower here because each regenerates the demo scenes). Ordinary development commands keep their own settings.

Release builds on memory-constrained machines: #1196 reports Arch/AUR release-link OOM kills on a 16 GB machine when the desktop and CLI build concurrently with full debug information, thin LTO and one codegen unit. The CI defaults above do not apply to ordinary cargo build --release. Start with one job; two may be suitable if enough memory is available:

CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli
# Alternatively: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli

If a packaging environment enables full debug information or memory-heavy LTO settings, use command-local overrides for a lower-memory source build:

CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 cargo build --release -p lightcraft -p lightcraft-cli

These POSIX-shell assignments affect only this command, not global Cargo configuration or the repository's release profiles. Disabling LTO may change performance and binary size; disabling debug information reduces debugging detail. This is build guidance, not a guarantee that any machine has enough memory. Downstream packagers should serialize large binary builds and avoid full debug information combined with LTO and one codegen unit on low-memory builders. A PKGBUILD that exports its own profile settings can override inherited variables; adjust the packaging recipe locally or contact its maintainer rather than assuming an environment prefix on makepkg will take precedence.

Linux/Arch build troubleshooting: rustc SIGILL with ThinLTO. In #2811, an Arch Linux x86_64 build on an AMD Ryzen 9 7900X3D with 64 GB RAM failed with rustc 1.99.0 / LLVM 23.1.1, AUR lightcraft 0.7.1-1 and 0.13.0-1, RUSTFLAGS="-C opt-level=3 -C target-cpu=native", and release settings opt-level=3, lto=thin, codegen-units=1. cargo build --frozen --release reached the executable crates before rustc crashed with signal 4 (SIGILL / ILL_ILLOPN). The core dumps point into LLVM's SelectionDAG / vector-combine optimization path; the exact compiler root cause has not been isolated. This does not mean every machine with that hardware or toolchain will fail. It is a different observed failure from the 16 GB OOM kills in #1196 above; there is no evidence establishing a shared root cause.

For a direct Cargo source build, the equivalent command-local LTO override is:

CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off cargo build --frozen --release

Reporter @rwarmstr verified the workaround by exporting CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off inside the AUR PKGBUILD's _srcenv() function and rebuilding both package versions, without changing RUSTFLAGS. The reporter tested the AUR recipe, not the direct Cargo invocation above. A variable prefixed to makepkg alone may be overwritten by the PKGBUILD's own exports; the recipe must honor or set the override. The AUR !lto opt-out behavior is tracked separately in #2813.

Cargo's LTO documentation distinguishes false from off: false can still perform thin local LTO across codegen units (unless codegen-units=1 or opt-level=0); off disables LTO explicitly. The low-memory recipe above is unchanged. This workaround is for affected builds, not a new default; disabling LTO may change performance, binary size and build behavior.

Tests that need a GPU, the corpus, the craft-fonts faces or a model pass without checking anything when those are missing (libtest has no "skipped" status), so cargo xtask ci lists them: tests record a skip with lightcraft_testkit::skip!, and the run ends with what the machine offered (OS, CPUs, RAM, GPU adapters per backend, corpus, fonts) and every skip by reason. It writes target/ci/report.json and target/ci/summary.md, a block to paste into a PR (--summary-md prints it); --hardware also runs the GPU tests on every backend that has a hardware adapter. Nothing is uploaded.

Chinese and Japanese text need the shared font repo, an optional build input (official releases always include it):

git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts ../craft-fonts
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo run --release -p lightcraft

Without it LightCraft builds and runs the same, but Chinese and Japanese text have no glyphs. Fonts are never committed to this repo — what goes there is described in the craft-fonts README.

Interface language: Edit → Language (English, 简体中文, 繁體中文（台灣）, 日本語, Português (Brasil), Español, Deutsch, Русский, Français, Українська, Polski, Čeština, Italiano, ქართული, Svenska, Suomi, Bahasa Indonesia, Tiếng Việt) or Settings → General → Language; the choice applies immediately and persists. See docs/localization.md.
